title: 16-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Dual-Band Filter with Expanded Bounds and Random Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with thickness bounds relaxed by ±8% from quarter-wave values and uniform random initialization will escape the local minimum observed in iteration_04, achieving higher dual-band performance through non-quarter-wave optimization.
design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector principle for UV band (200-400 nm) with non-quarter-wave thickness optimization to maintain SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm). Random initialization prevents convergence to the same local basin as prior deterministic runs.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (16 finite layers, 8 pairs)
design_variables: Thickness bounds: quarter-wave ±8% at 300 nm center UV wavelength
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Minimize spectral ripple in both bands
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are deposition-compatible via ion-assisted deposition
Outermost SiO2 layer provides environmental durability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: ±8% bounds allow escape from quarter-wave local minimum
Random initialization increases design space exploration
known_risks: May converge to similar local minimum as iteration_04 if bounds too restrictive
16 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous UV reflection and SWIR transmission optimization
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on fused silica substrate for dual-band performance. Layer sequence: HfO2/SiO2 repeated 8 times starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize all layer thicknesses with uniform random sampling within bounds: HfO2 layers 38-45 nm, SiO2 layers 47-55 nm (quarter-wave at 300 nm ±8%). Optimize thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with Adam-LBFGS hybrid. Spectral evaluation: 200-1500 nm with 1 nm resolution. Objectives: maximize mean transmittance 800-1500 nm, maximize mean reflectance 200-400 nm. Total layer count fixed at 16. Material registry resolves HfO2 and SiO2 refractive indices. If best_target_score improvement < 1e-3 for 4 consecutive iterations, trigger Monte Carlo resampling of thickness initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Refinement of iteration_04 16-layer design: expanded thickness bounds by ±8%, switched from deterministic grid initialization to uniform random sampling per feedback directives, added Monte Carlo resampling checkpoint to escape local minima.
